questions.stem: A map uses red for "above average" and green for "below average". Which revision keeps the meaning clear for readers with color-vision deficiency and in a black-and-white printout?
choices: Switch to pink for above and light green for below
Use two colors of very different lightness, with labels
Keep red and green and add a thicker border around each region
Keep red and green and make the whole map larger
questions.answer: Use two colors of very different lightness, with labels
questions.solution: In black and white, only differences in lightness remain, and readers with color-vision deficiency may not tell red from green. Colors that differ strongly in lightness, with labels as a back-up, stay clear. Pink and light green can be close in lightness and give no back-up, and borders or size do not change the colors.

solve.answer: Use two colors of very different lightness, with labels
solve.work: Very different lightness survives color-vision deficiency and grayscale printing, and labels make meaning explicit. Pink/light green remains a red-green pair; size/borders do not fix it.

questions.stem: A pie chart has 14 slices of similar sizes, with a color key to name them. Which revision makes it easiest to compare the categories?
choices: The same pie chart with 14 brighter colors in the key
A 3-D pie chart, so that each of the slices looks bigger
The same pie chart with the slices in a random order
A sorted bar chart with the categories labeled directly
questions.answer: A sorted bar chart with the categories labeled directly
questions.solution: People compare lengths along a common line better than angles or areas, especially when many slices are alike. A sorted bar chart with direct labels also removes the key.

solve.answer: A sorted bar chart with the categories labeled directly
solve.work: Many similar slices are hard to compare by angle; a sorted bar chart with direct labels allows comparing lengths and removes the key. 3-D distorts; random order and brighter colors do not help.

questions.stem: A graph shows only the mean household income, 80,000 dollars, of 10 households in a small town. Nine of the households have an income of exactly 50,000 dollars each. What is the income, in dollars, of the tenth household?
questions.solution: The 10 incomes total $10 \times 80000 = 800000$ dollars. Nine of them total $9 \times 50000 = 450000$. The tenth is $800000 - 450000 = 350000$ dollars. The mean (80,000) is far above what 9 of the 10 households earn, so it is not a typical income.

questions.skill: Bar chart axis that does not start at zero
questions.stem: A bar chart's vertical axis starts at 80 instead of 0. Measured from the start of the axis, bar A looks 3 times as tall as bar B. Bar B shows a value of 85. What value does bar A show?
questions.solution: Bar B is drawn $85 - 80 = 5$ units tall, so bar A is drawn $3 \times 5 = 15$ units tall. Bar A shows $80 + 15 = 95$.

solve.work: B drawn height = 85 - 80 = 5. A drawn height = 3 x 5 = 15. A value = 80 + 15 = 95.

questions.stem: A bar graph shows that 55% of residents support a plan and 45% oppose it, and the bars look very different. A footnote says the survey asked only 20 people and gives no margin of error. Which is the best critique?
choices: With only 20 people, the split could be chance; show the uncertainty
The graph is fine, because the two percentages add up to exactly 100%
The percentages would be better drawn as slices of a pie chart
A graph of support is only valid if the support is above 60%
questions.answer: With only 20 people, the split could be chance; show the uncertainty
questions.solution: With 20 people, the sample proportion can easily differ from the true one by 10 points or more, so 55% versus 45% is not a reliable difference. A good graphic reports the sample size and the uncertainty.

solve.answer: With only 20 people, the split could be chance; show the uncertainty
solve.work: With n = 20 the split is 11 vs 9; the margin of error is large (about 22 points), so the difference could be chance. The best critique is to show the uncertainty. Other options are irrelevant or false.

questions.skill: Bar chart axis that does not start at zero
questions.stem: A bar chart has a vertical axis that starts at 50. One bar shows 80 and another shows 65. Measured from the start of the axis, the shorter bar is what fraction of the taller bar's height?
questions.solution: The bars are $80 - 50 = 30$ and $65 - 50 = 15$ units tall. The shorter bar is $\frac{15}{30} = \frac{1}{2}$ of the taller, although 65 is more than 80 percent of 80.

questions.skill: Bar chart axis that does not start at zero
questions.stem: A designer starts a bar chart's axis at 90, saying, "The value is printed on every bar, so nothing is hidden." Which is the best response?
choices: Readers judge bar lengths first, which suggest ratios the values do not have
The printed values prove that readers are never misled by the bars
Bar charts are always misleading unless every bar has a printed value
The axis start changes only the colors and the width of the bars
questions.answer: Readers judge bar lengths first, which suggest ratios the values do not have
questions.solution: People compare the lengths of the bars at a glance, and a truncated axis makes the lengths misrepresent the ratios of the values, whatever labels are printed.

solve.answer: Readers judge bar lengths first, which suggest ratios the values do not have
solve.work: Readers judge lengths, so a truncated axis implies false ratios despite printed values.

questions.skill: Axis range and shape of a line graph
questions.stem: A line graph has a vertical axis that runs from 0 to 80 over a height of 4 centimeters, and a horizontal axis that shows 10 years over a width of 10 centimeters. A line goes from the value 20 at the start to the value 60 at the end of the 10 years. What is the slope of the drawn line, in centimeters up per centimeter across?
questions.solution: The rise of $60 - 20 = 40$ units is $\frac{40}{80} \times 4 = 2$ centimeters on the page. The run is 10 centimeters. The drawn slope is $\frac{2}{10} = \frac{1}{5}$.

solve.work: Vertical: 80 units over 4 cm = 20 units/cm; rise 40 -> 2 cm. Across 10 cm. Slope 2/10 = 0.2.

questions.skill: Axis range and shape of a line graph
questions.stem: A line graph of a town's yearly growth is redrawn four times as wide, with the same height and the same axes. How does the growth appear on the redrawn graph?
choices: Steeper, so the growth looks faster
Flatter, so the same growth looks slower
Exactly the same as it looked before it was widened
The growth is shown as a smaller number
questions.answer: Flatter, so the same growth looks slower
questions.solution: Stretching the graph sideways spreads each year over more width while the rise stays the same height, so the line slopes less. The data are unchanged, but the impression differs.

solve.answer: Flatter, so the same growth looks slower
solve.work: Same rise over 4 times the width -> flatter.

questions.skill: Axis range and shape of a line graph
questions.stem: Company X's stock rose from 10 to 12 dollars and Company Y's stock rose from 200 to 220 dollars. Both are drawn as lines on one graph with the axis from 0 to 250. What is the best way to compare how fast they grew?
choices: Keep the axis from 0 to 250 so that the prices are comparable
Use a different vertical axis for each company without labels
Plot percent change from the start, or an index set to 100
Show only the company whose price ended higher
questions.answer: Plot percent change from the start, or an index set to 100
questions.solution: On one dollar axis, Company X looks flat because its price is small. Percent change (20 percent for X and 10 percent for Y) or an index puts both on a common scale for growth.

solve.answer: Plot percent change from the start, or an index set to 100
solve.work: X grew 20%, Y 10%; compare relative change via percent change or index.

questions.stem: On a graph with a logarithmic scale, 1 centimeter along the axis stands for multiplying a quantity by 10. A line on the graph rises exactly 2 centimeters each year. By what factor does the quantity grow in 3 years?
questions.solution: In 3 years the line rises $2 \times 3 = 6$ centimeters. Each centimeter is a factor of 10, so the quantity is multiplied by $10^6 = 1{,}000{,}000$.

solve.work: 2 cm per year = factor 100 per year; 3 years: 100^3 = 1,000,000.

questions.stem: A designer picks the range of each of two vertical axes so that two lines move almost together. What does this show about the data?
choices: The two quantities are strongly related to each other
That one quantity causes changes in the other quantity
The two quantities were measured in the same units
Nothing, because the match depends on the axis ranges
questions.answer: Nothing, because the match depends on the axis ranges
questions.solution: With a free choice of ranges on two axes, almost any two series can be made to look alike. A close match on such a graph is no evidence of a relationship.

solve.answer: Nothing, because the match depends on the axis ranges
solve.work: Chosen axis ranges can force lines together; the match itself shows nothing.

questions.stem: On a graph with a logarithmic vertical axis, a line is straight and rises. What does this say about the quantity?
choices: It grows by the same factor in each equal time step
It grows by the same amount in each of the equal time steps
It stays the same over time
It grows more and more slowly
questions.answer: It grows by the same factor in each equal time step
questions.solution: A straight line on a log scale means equal steps in time give equal multiplying factors. That is exponential growth, such as a doubling every year.

solve.answer: It grows by the same factor in each equal time step
solve.work: Straight rising line on log axis = constant growth factor (exponential).

questions.stem: A stacked bar chart splits each of 6 bars into four colored segments. A reader wants to compare one segment's size across all the bars. Which segment is easiest to compare?
choices: The segment in the middle, because it is surrounded by two other segments
The bottom segment, because all of them start at the same baseline
The segment at the top, because it is the last one drawn on each bar
All the segments are equally easy to compare
questions.answer: The bottom segment, because all of them start at the same baseline
questions.solution: Only the bottom segment starts at the common baseline, so its lengths can be compared directly. The other segments start at different heights, which makes comparison harder.

solve.answer: The bottom segment, because all of them start at the same baseline
solve.work: Only the bottom segments share a common baseline.

questions.stem: A heat map uses a rainbow of colors, from purple through blue, green and yellow to red, to show the values from low to high. What is a problem with this?
choices: Rainbow colors can only show two or three different values at a time
Rainbow colors cannot be printed in a report in any way
The colors have no natural order and look uneven in brightness
The color key would have to show the numbers, which is not allowed
questions.answer: The colors have no natural order and look uneven in brightness
questions.solution: A rainbow has no obvious low-to-high order, and some bands look brighter or wider than others, so equal steps in the data can look uneven. A single hue from light to dark is better.

solve.answer: The colors have no natural order and look uneven in brightness
solve.work: Rainbow has no perceptual order and uneven lightness.

questions.stem: A bar chart has 12 bars, one for each region, and the story is about Region C. How should color be used?
choices: Give each of the 12 bars its own bright color so all stand out
Make Region C gray and make all of the other bars bright
Use the same color for all the bars so none stands out
Use a strong color for Region C and a muted gray for the other bars
questions.answer: Use a strong color for Region C and a muted gray for the other bars
questions.solution: Color should direct attention. A single strong color against a muted background leads the reader to Region C and keeps the others available for comparison.

solve.answer: Use a strong color for Region C and a muted gray for the other bars
solve.work: Highlight the focus bar, mute the rest.

questions.skill: What averages, bins and aggregation hide
questions.stem: Class 1 has 40 students with a pass rate of 90%. Class 2 has 10 students with a pass rate of 40%. A single bar shows the pass rate of all 50 students together. What percent is shown? Enter the number without the percent sign.
questions.solution: Class 1 has $0.9 \times 40 = 36$ passes and Class 2 has $0.4 \times 10 = 4$ passes, 40 in all. The combined rate is $\frac{40}{50} \times 100 = 80$ percent. The single bar hides that the two classes differ greatly.

questions.skill: What averages, bins and aggregation hide
questions.stem: A graph of daily website visits shows a 7-day moving average instead of the daily values. What does the smoothed line hide?
choices: One-day spikes or dips, which are averaged away
Whether the visits rose steadily over several months
The overall level of the visits during the 7 days
The units that the visits are counted in each day
questions.answer: One-day spikes or dips, which are averaged away
questions.solution: A moving average mixes each day with its neighbors, so a single-day spike is spread out and looks small, though it helps to show the long-term trend.

solve.answer: One-day spikes or dips, which are averaged away
solve.work: A 7-day average smooths out single-day spikes and dips.

questions.skill: What averages, bins and aggregation hide
questions.stem: A histogram has bins 0 to 10, 10 to 20 and 20 to 50. Its bar heights are the counts: 20, 20 and 30. What is misleading about it?
choices: The bin 0 to 10 should be drawn taller than the other two bins
The widest bin looks too big; heights should be counts per unit width
The counts should have been added together to make one single bar
Histograms must use bins that all have exactly the same count
questions.answer: The widest bin looks too big; heights should be counts per unit width
questions.solution: A bar's area should stand for its count. With unequal bin widths, the heights should be the count per unit of width, so that the wide bin does not seem to hold more than it does.

solve.answer: The widest bin looks too big; heights should be counts per unit width
solve.work: The 20-50 bin is 3 times as wide; with count heights its area overstates it; use density (count per unit width): 30/30 = 1 vs 2 for others.

questions.skill: What averages, bins and aggregation hide
questions.stem: A map shades each state by its total number of flu cases, and the darkest states are those with the most people. What is the best revision?
choices: Shade by the number of counties that each state contains
Use the same color for all states so none stands out
Shade by the rate of cases per 100,000 people, not the total
List the states in alphabetical order beside the map
questions.answer: Shade by the rate of cases per 100,000 people, not the total
questions.solution: A state with more people will usually have more cases, so totals mostly show population. A rate per 100,000 people allows a fair comparison.

solve.answer: Shade by the rate of cases per 100,000 people, not the total
solve.work: Totals mirror population; use a per-capita rate.

questions.stem: A stem-and-leaf plot has stem 1 with leaves 2, 5 and 8; stem 2 with leaves 0, 3, 3 and 7; and stem 3 with leaves 1 and 4. A leaf is the ones digit of a value, so stem 1 and leaf 2 is 12. How many values are greater than 25?
questions.solution: The values are 12, 15, 18, 20, 23, 23, 27, 31 and 34. The values greater than 25 are 27, 31 and 34, which is 3 values. A stem-and-leaf plot keeps every value visible.

questions.stem: Which question is a histogram better than a box plot at answering?
choices: What is the median of the data?
What is the interquartile range of the data?
What is the smallest value?
Does the data have two separate peaks?
questions.answer: Does the data have two separate peaks?
questions.solution: A box plot shows only a five-number summary, so it cannot show two peaks. A histogram shows the full shape, including peaks and gaps.

solve.answer: Does the data have two separate peaks?
solve.work: A box plot hides bimodality; a histogram shows it.

questions.stem: A scatterplot of 3,000 points is so crowded that many points lie on top of each other. Which revision helps most?
choices: Make the points small and partly see-through
Make every point larger and fully solid in one color
Remove the axes and their labels to save space
Draw each of the points in a random color
questions.answer: Make the points small and partly see-through
questions.solution: Overlapping points hide how many there are. Small, semi-transparent points show density, because places with many points look darker.

solve.answer: Make the points small and partly see-through
solve.work: Small, semi-transparent points reveal density in overplotting.

questions.stem: A report shows three graphs, one for each of three schools. Each has a different vertical axis range, so the graphs are hard to compare. What is the best revision?
choices: Give each graph its own different color scheme
Give all three graphs the same axis range, side by side
Remove the vertical axis from two of the graphs
Combine the three graphs into a single pie chart
questions.answer: Give all three graphs the same axis range, side by side
questions.solution: Graphs meant for comparison should share a scale. With the same axis range, equal heights mean equal values in all three.

solve.answer: Give all three graphs the same axis range, side by side
solve.work: Common scales side by side allow comparison.

questions.stem: A bar chart shows enrollment rising from 400 students in 2015 to 650 in 2024. Which text is best as its description for a screen reader?
choices: A bar chart with bars of two colors
A picture of the enrollment data for the school
Bar chart: enrollment rises from 400 in 2015 to 650 in 2024
Bars in blue and orange with a gray background
questions.answer: Bar chart: enrollment rises from 400 in 2015 to 650 in 2024
questions.solution: A useful description gives the kind of chart and the main finding with the numbers, so a reader who cannot see it still learns what it shows.

solve.answer: Bar chart: enrollment rises from 400 in 2015 to 650 in 2024
solve.work: Alt text should convey the message and values.

questions.stem: A published graph shows that ice cream sales and drowning cases both rise and fall together over the months, and its headline says, "Ice cream causes drowning." Which is the best critique?
choices: The graph proves it, because the two lines match so closely
The graph should have used a pie chart instead of lines
The headline is correct if the axes start at 0
A third factor, such as hot weather, may cause both of them
questions.answer: A third factor, such as hot weather, may cause both of them
questions.solution: Two series that move together need not cause each other. Hot weather increases both ice cream sales and swimming, so a link in a graph is not evidence of cause.

solve.answer: A third factor, such as hot weather, may cause both of them
solve.work: Correlation not causation; hot weather is a lurking variable.

questions.stem: A graph titled "Typical income" shows the mean income of a country, where a few people have extremely high incomes. What is the best improvement?
choices: Show the median, since the mean is pulled up by the high incomes
Show the largest income, since it is the most interesting
Keep the mean, since a mean is always the typical value
Show the sum of all the incomes in the country
questions.answer: Show the median, since the mean is pulled up by the high incomes
questions.solution: Extremely high incomes raise the mean above what most people earn. The median is resistant to them, so it better describes a typical income.

solve.answer: Show the median, since the mean is pulled up by the high incomes
solve.work: Skewed incomes: median is the typical value.

questions.stem: A city's graph shows thefts falling from 40 to 20 in a year, under the headline "Crime cut in half!". Over the same year, the city's population fell from 100,000 to 50,000. How many thefts per 10,000 residents occurred this year?
questions.solution: The rate this year is $\frac{20}{50{,}000} \times 10{,}000 = 4$ thefts per 10,000 residents. Last year it was $\frac{40}{100{,}000} \times 10{,}000 = 4$ also, so the rate did not change.

solve.work: This year: 20 thefts / 50,000 residents x 10,000 = 4 (the same rate as last year, 40/100,000).

questions.stem: Five friends read 6, 8, 9, 10 and 12 books this year. What is the mean number of books they read?
questions.solution: Add the values: 6 + 8 + 9 + 10 + 12 = 45. Divide by the 5 values: 45 / 5 = 9.

questions.stem: The ages of five players on a team are 14, 9, 11, 15 and 12. What is the median age?
questions.solution: Put the ages in order: 9, 11, 12, 14, 15. The middle value of the five is 12.

solve.work: Sorted: 9, 11, 12, 14, 15. Middle (3rd) value = 12.

questions.stem: Five quiz scores are 72, 85, 64, 90 and 78. What is the range of the scores?
questions.solution: The range is the largest value minus the smallest value: 90 - 64 = 26.

solve.work: Max 90, min 64; range = 90 - 64 = 26.

questions.stem: A test has a mean of 70 and a standard deviation of 5. Dana scored 85. What is her z-score?
questions.solution: The z-score is (score - mean) / standard deviation = (85 - 70) / 5 = 15 / 5 = 3. Dana scored 3 standard deviations above the mean.

questions.stem: A group of 250 students took a test. Mia's score was at the 80th percentile. About how many students scored at or below Mia's score?
questions.solution: The 80th percentile means about 80% of the scores are at or below hers: 0.80 x 250 = 200 students.

solve.work: 80th percentile: about 80% at or below. 0.8 x 250 = 200.

questions.stem: A data set has one very large outlier. Which summary is least affected by the outlier?
choices: The mean
The median
The range
The standard deviation
questions.answer: The median
questions.solution: The median depends only on the middle of the ordered data, so one extreme value barely changes it. The mean, the range and the standard deviation all change a lot when a value is far from the rest.

solve.answer: The median
solve.work: The median depends only on the middle position, so one extreme value barely moves it; mean, SD and range all change with the outlier.

questions.stem: The mean number of text messages sent per day by the students in a class is 42. Which is the best interpretation of this mean?
choices: Half of the students send more than 42 messages per day, and half fewer
The most common number of messages sent by one student per day is 42
Every student in the class sends exactly 42 messages every day
If the messages were shared out equally, each student would send 42
questions.answer: If the messages were shared out equally, each student would send 42
questions.solution: The mean is the total shared out equally among all the students. It does not say that half the students are above it (that is the median), what is most common (the mode), or that everyone sent the same amount.

solve.answer: If the messages were shared out equally, each student would send 42
solve.work: The mean is the fair-share value: total messages divided equally gives 42 each. 'Half above/below' is the median; 'most common' is the mode.

questions.stem: What does the standard deviation of a data set measure?
choices: How far the values typically are from the mean
The middle value of the data
The difference between the largest and smallest values
The value that occurs most often
questions.answer: How far the values typically are from the mean
questions.solution: The standard deviation measures how spread out the values are around the mean. The middle value is the median, the largest minus the smallest is the range, and the most frequent value is the mode.

solve.answer: How far the values typically are from the mean
solve.work: Standard deviation measures the typical distance of values from the mean.

questions.stem: Which of these is a measure of spread, not a measure of center?
choices: The mean
The median
The range
The mode
questions.answer: The range
questions.solution: The mean, the median and the mode all describe the center of the data. The range (largest value minus smallest value) describes how spread out the data are.

solve.answer: The range
solve.work: Mean, mode and median are centre; range is spread.

questions.stem: Class A and Class B both have a mean quiz score of 80. Class A has a standard deviation of 4 and Class B has a standard deviation of 12. Which statement is true?
choices: Class B's scores are clustered more closely around 80
Class B's students scored higher than Class A's students
Class A's scores are clustered more closely around 80
Class A scored higher than Class B on average
questions.answer: Class A's scores are clustered more closely around 80
questions.solution: The means are equal, so neither class scored higher on average. The smaller standard deviation belongs to Class A, so its scores are closer to 80 and more consistent.

solve.answer: Class A's scores are clustered more closely around 80
solve.work: Same mean, so neither scored higher on average. Smaller SD (Class A, 4) means scores cluster more closely around 80.

questions.stem: The mean of 5 numbers is 12. What is the sum of the 5 numbers?
questions.solution: The mean is the sum divided by the number of values, so the sum is the mean times the number of values: $5 \times 12 = 60$.

questions.stem: A team scored 2, 5, 1, 4, 3, 0 and 6 goals in 7 games. What is the median number of goals?
questions.solution: Put the values in order: 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6. The middle (fourth) value is 3.

solve.work: Sorted 0,1,2,3,4,5,6; middle (4th) = 3.

questions.stem: A data set in order from least to greatest is 4, 6, 9, 12, 20. The first quartile is the median of the lower half, leaving out the median of the whole set. What is the first quartile?
questions.solution: The median is 9, so the lower half is 4 and 6. Their median is $\frac{4+6}{2} = 5$.

solve.work: Lower half 4, 6 -> Q1 = 5.

questions.stem: A data set has a first quartile of 20 and a third quartile of 35. What is its interquartile range?
questions.solution: The interquartile range is the third quartile minus the first: $35 - 20 = 15$.

questions.stem: Which data set has a standard deviation of exactly 0?
questions.solution: The standard deviation is 0 only when no value differs from the mean, so all the values must be equal. Only 4, 4, 4, 4 qualifies.

solve.work: All values equal -> no deviation -> SD 0.

questions.stem: The heights of some children are measured in centimeters. In what unit is the standard deviation of their heights measured?
choices: Square centimeters
Percent
No unit, because it is a pure number
Centimeters
questions.answer: Centimeters
questions.solution: The standard deviation is a typical distance from the mean, so it has the same unit as the data: centimeters. The variance, not the standard deviation, is in square centimeters.

solve.answer: Centimeters
solve.work: SD is in the same unit as the data: centimeters.

questions.stem: On a quiz the mean score is 50 and the standard deviation is 10. Sam scored 70. What is Sam's z-score?
questions.solution: $z = \frac{70 - 50}{10} = 2$. Sam's score is 2 standard deviations above the mean.

questions.stem: A value in a data set has a z-score of $-1$. What does this tell you?
choices: The value is 1 standard deviation below the mean
The value is 1 unit of measurement below the mean value
The value is 1 percent below the mean
The value is 1 standard deviation above the mean
questions.answer: The value is 1 standard deviation below the mean
questions.solution: A z-score counts standard deviations from the mean, and the sign gives the direction. A z-score of $-1$ is 1 standard deviation below the mean.

solve.answer: The value is 1 standard deviation below the mean
solve.work: z = -1 means one SD below the mean.

questions.stem: Which of these z-scores belongs to a value that is above the mean?
questions.solution: A positive z-score means a value above the mean. A z-score of 0 is at the mean and negative z-scores are below it.

solve.work: Positive z is above the mean: 1.5.

questions.stem: A student's test score is at the 25th percentile. What does this mean?
choices: The student answered 25% of the questions on the test correctly
About 25% of the students scored above this particular score
About 25% of the students scored at or below this score
The student scored exactly 25 points out of 100 on the test
questions.answer: About 25% of the students scored at or below this score
questions.solution: A percentile tells the percent of the group at or below the value. The 25th percentile means about 25% scored at or below it.

solve.answer: About 25% of the students scored at or below this score
solve.work: 25th percentile: about 25% scored at or below.

questions.stem: Of 200 students who took a test, 150 scored at or below Jo's score. Jo's score is at what percentile?
questions.solution: The percentile is the percent of the group at or below the score: $\frac{150}{200} \times 100 = 75$, so the 75th percentile.

questions.stem: Which pair of summaries is NOT changed much by a single extreme outlier?
choices: The mean and the standard deviation
The mean and the range
The range and the standard deviation
The median and the interquartile range
questions.answer: The median and the interquartile range
questions.solution: The median and the interquartile range depend on the middle of the ordered data, so one extreme value barely moves them. The mean, standard deviation and range all use the extreme value.

solve.answer: The median and the interquartile range
solve.work: Median and IQR are resistant.

questions.stem: Five test scores are 10, 12, 14, 16 and 18, with a mean of 14. If the 18 is changed to 58, what is the new mean?
questions.solution: The new total is $10 + 12 + 14 + 16 + 58 = 110$, and $110 \div 5 = 22$. One large value raised the mean from 14 to 22.

questions.stem: Team X has a median score of 12 points and Team Y has a median score of 15 points. Which statement is supported?
choices: Team X's scores are more spread out than Team Y's
Team Y's typical score is higher than Team X's
Every score of Team Y is higher than every score of Team X
Team Y's scores are more spread out than Team X's
questions.answer: Team Y's typical score is higher than Team X's
questions.solution: A median describes a typical value, so the higher median means a higher typical score. It says nothing about spread, and it does not mean every score is higher.

solve.answer: Team Y's typical score is higher than Team X's
solve.work: Median describes a typical score; 15 > 12. Medians say nothing of spread or every score.

questions.stem: Data set P has a range of 10 and data set Q has a range of 40. Which statement is true?
choices: The mean of Q is larger than the mean of P
The median of P is smaller than the median of Q
Q's values cover a wider interval than P's
Data set P has more values than data set Q
questions.answer: Q's values cover a wider interval than P's
questions.solution: The range measures how far the largest value is from the smallest. A larger range means the values are spread over a wider interval; it says nothing about the means or medians.

solve.answer: Q's values cover a wider interval than P's
solve.work: Range is max minus min; larger range = wider interval. Nothing about means, size, medians.

questions.stem: A distribution has a long tail that stretches toward the larger values. How is it described?
choices: Skewed to the left
Symmetric
Uniform
Skewed to the right
questions.answer: Skewed to the right
questions.solution: A distribution is named for the side its tail is on. A long tail toward the larger values is skewed to the right.

solve.answer: Skewed to the right
solve.work: Tail toward large values = right skew.

questions.stem: Heights measured in feet have a mean of 5. Each height is converted to inches, where 1 foot is 12 inches. What is the mean height in inches?
questions.solution: Multiplying every value by 12 multiplies the mean by 12: $5 \times 12 = 60$ inches.

questions.stem: The median commute time of the workers at a company is 25 minutes. Which interpretation is correct?
choices: About half of the workers commute 25 minutes or less
Every worker commutes exactly 25 minutes
About 25% of the workers commute to work
The commute times of all the workers add up to 25 minutes
questions.answer: About half of the workers commute 25 minutes or less
questions.solution: The median is the middle value, so about half of the workers have a commute at or below it and about half at or above it.

solve.answer: About half of the workers commute 25 minutes or less
solve.work: Median: about half at or below 25.

questions.stem: A survey records the number of children in 10 families. Three families have 1 child, five families have 2 children and two families have 4 children. What is the mean number of children per family?
questions.solution: The total number of children is $3\times 1+5\times 2+2\times 4=3+10+8=21$. Divide by the 10 families: $21\div 10=2.1$.

solve.work: Total children = 3*1 + 5*2 + 2*4 = 3 + 10 + 8 = 21 across 10 families. Mean = 21/10 = 2.1.

questions.stem: Two classes took the same test, and both classes have a mean score of 75. The standard deviation of Class A is 4 and the standard deviation of Class B is 12. Which statement is best supported?
choices: Class A has more spread out scores, because its standard deviation is smaller
Both classes have equally spread out scores, because their means are equal
Class B has more spread out scores, because its standard deviation is larger
Neither class can be judged, because the class sizes are not given
questions.answer: Class B has more spread out scores, because its standard deviation is larger
questions.solution: The standard deviation measures spread, so the class with the larger standard deviation has the more spread out scores. That is Class B. The means say nothing about spread, and the class sizes are not needed to compare the two standard deviations.

solve.answer: Class B has more spread out scores, because its standard deviation is larger
solve.work: Equal means; standard deviation measures spread, so Class B (SD 12) is more spread out than Class A (SD 4). Class sizes are not needed for this comparison.

questions.stem: A data set has 20 values. About how many of the values lie between the first quartile and the third quartile?
questions.solution: A quarter of the values are at or below the first quartile and a quarter are at or above the third quartile. That leaves the middle half of the values between them: $20\div 2=10$ values.

solve.work: The middle 50% of the data lies between Q1 and Q3: about half of 20 = 10 values.

questions.stem: A data set has an interquartile range of 12. Every value in the data set is multiplied by 3. What is the interquartile range of the new data set?
questions.solution: Multiplying every value by 3 stretches every distance between values by a factor of 3, so the quartiles and their difference are multiplied by 3 too: $12\times 3=36$.

solve.work: Multiplying every value by 3 multiplies both quartiles by 3, so the IQR becomes 3*12 = 36.

questions.stem: Which data set is best described by its mean, rather than by its median?
choices: Home prices in a town with a few very expensive mansions
Salaries at a firm where two owners earn far more than the rest
Quiz scores that are roughly symmetric with no outliers
Waiting times that include a few extremely long delays
questions.answer: Quiz scores that are roughly symmetric with no outliers
questions.solution: The mean is pulled toward extreme values, so it describes a typical value well only when the data are roughly symmetric with no outliers. The other three sets are skewed by a few extreme values, and the median describes them better.

solve.answer: Quiz scores that are roughly symmetric with no outliers
solve.work: The mean suits a symmetric distribution without outliers; the other three are skewed by extreme values, where the median is better. Answer: the symmetric quiz scores.

questions.stem: A shop counted its customers in each of eight hours: 5, 7, 8, 12, 3, 9, 10 and 6. What is the median number of customers per hour?
questions.solution: Put the counts in order: 3, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 12. With 8 values the median is the mean of the 4th and 5th: (7 + 8) / 2 = 7.5.

questions.stem: Eight students spent 1, 3, 4, 6, 7, 9, 10 and 14 minutes on homework. Find the quartiles as the medians of the lower four values and the upper four values. What is the interquartile range?
questions.solution: The lower four values are 1, 3, 4, 6, so Q1 = (3 + 4) / 2 = 3.5. The upper four values are 7, 9, 10, 14, so Q3 = (9 + 10) / 2 = 9.5. The interquartile range is Q3 - Q1 = 9.5 - 3.5 = 6.

questions.stem: Three plant heights, in centimeters, are 4, 8 and 12. Treat them as a sample and find the sample standard deviation: divide the sum of the squared deviations from the mean by $n - 1$, then take the square root. What is the standard deviation?
questions.solution: The mean is (4 + 8 + 12) / 3 = 8. The squared deviations are 16, 0 and 16, with sum 32. Divide by n - 1 = 2 to get 16, and the square root of 16 is 4.

questions.stem: On a test the mean score is 64 and the standard deviation is 8. One student has a z-score of -1.5. What was that student's score?
questions.solution: A z-score of -1.5 means 1.5 standard deviations below the mean: 1.5 x 8 = 12 points below 64, so the score is 64 - 12 = 52.

questions.stem: The mean of a student's first five test scores is 82. A sixth score of 94 is added. What is the mean of all six scores?
questions.solution: The first five scores total 5 x 82 = 410. Adding 94 gives 504. Divide by 6: 504 / 6 = 84.

questions.stem: A data set of 9 values has a mean of 30 and a median of 30. The largest value is then replaced by a value that is 100 higher. What happens?
choices: The mean increases by about 11, and the median stays at 30
The mean increases by the full 100, and the median stays at 30
The mean stays at 30, and the median increases by about 11
The mean and the median both increase by about 11
questions.answer: The mean increases by about 11, and the median stays at 30
questions.solution: The total goes up by 100, shared over 9 values, so the mean rises by 100 / 9, about 11. The median is the 5th value in order, and raising the largest value does not change which value is in the middle.

solve.answer: The mean increases by about 11, and the median stays at 30
solve.work: Sum rises by 100, so mean rises by 100/9 = 11.1, about 11. The largest value stays the largest; the 5th of 9 ordered values (median) is unchanged at 30.

questions.stem: The prices of homes in a city are strongly skewed to the right because of a few very expensive mansions. Which pair of summaries best describes the typical price and the spread?
choices: The mean and the standard deviation of all the prices
The mean and the range of the prices
The mode and the standard deviation of the prices
The median and the interquartile range of the prices
questions.answer: The median and the interquartile range of the prices
questions.solution: For a skewed distribution with extreme values, the median and the interquartile range are resistant to the outliers. The mean, the standard deviation and the range are pulled by the mansions.

solve.answer: The median and the interquartile range of the prices
solve.work: For strongly skewed data with outliers, resistant summaries are best: median for centre, IQR for spread.

questions.stem: Group A has a median score of 70 and an interquartile range of 10. Group B has a median score of 78 and an interquartile range of 25. Which statement is correct?
choices: Group A typically scores higher, and Group A's scores are more spread out
Group B typically scores higher, and Group B's scores are more spread out
Group B typically scores higher, and Group A's scores are more spread out
Group A typically scores higher, and Group B's scores are more spread out
questions.answer: Group B typically scores higher, and Group B's scores are more spread out
questions.solution: The median measures the typical score, and Group B's median is higher. The interquartile range measures spread, and Group B's is larger, so its scores are more spread out.

solve.answer: Group B typically scores higher, and Group B's scores are more spread out
solve.work: B's median 78 > 70, so B typically higher; B's IQR 25 > 10, so B more spread out.

questions.stem: Ana's test score was at the 90th percentile. Which statement is correct?
choices: About 90% of the students scored at or below Ana's score
Ana answered 90% of the questions on the test correctly
About 90% of the students scored above Ana's score on the test
Ana's score on the test was exactly 90 points out of 100
questions.answer: About 90% of the students scored at or below Ana's score
questions.solution: A percentile tells the percent of values at or below a score. The 90th percentile means about 90% of students scored the same or lower, so only about 10% scored higher. It does not say what percent of the questions she answered correctly.

solve.answer: About 90% of the students scored at or below Ana's score
solve.work: 90th percentile: about 90% of scores are at or below hers. Not percent correct, not a score of 90.

questions.stem: The waiting times at a clinic had a mean of 12 minutes and a standard deviation of 3 minutes. Which is the best interpretation of the standard deviation?
choices: Every patient waited between 9 and 15 minutes, with no exceptions
The longest wait was exactly 3 minutes more than the shortest wait
Waiting times typically differ from the mean of 12 by about 3 minutes
The most common waiting time at the clinic was exactly 3 minutes
questions.answer: Waiting times typically differ from the mean of 12 by about 3 minutes
questions.solution: The standard deviation is a typical distance of the values from the mean. It does not set hard limits on the waits, it is not the range, and it is not the most frequent value.

solve.answer: Waiting times typically differ from the mean of 12 by about 3 minutes
solve.work: SD = typical distance from the mean: waits typically differ from 12 by about 3 minutes. Not a hard bound, not the mode, not the range.

questions.stem: The mean of 6 numbers is 20. When one of the numbers, 30, is removed, what is the mean of the remaining 5 numbers?
questions.solution: The sum of the 6 numbers is $6 \times 20 = 120$. Without the 30 the sum is $90$, and the mean of 5 numbers is $90 \div 5 = 18$.

questions.stem: In a class of 20 students, 5 have 0 pets, 8 have 1 pet, 6 have 2 pets and 1 has 3 pets. What is the mean number of pets per student?
questions.solution: The total number of pets is $0 \times 5 + 1 \times 8 + 2 \times 6 + 3 \times 1 = 23$. Divide by 20 students: $\frac{23}{20} = 1.15$.

questions.stem: Six students received 3, 8, 5, 9, 4 and 7 stickers. What is the median number of stickers?
questions.solution: In order the values are 3, 4, 5, 7, 8, 9. The two middle values are 5 and 7, and their mean is $\frac{5+7}{2} = 6$.

questions.stem: Nine values in order are 2, 4, 5, 7, 8, 10, 12, 13 and 20. Find the third quartile as the median of the upper half, leaving out the median of the whole set. What is the third quartile?
questions.solution: The median is the fifth value, 8. The upper half is 10, 12, 13, 20, and its median is $\frac{12+13}{2} = 12.5$.

questions.stem: Ten values in order are 3, 5, 6, 8, 9, 11, 12, 14, 15 and 20. Find the quartiles as the medians of the lower five values and the upper five values. What is the interquartile range?
questions.solution: The lower five values are 3, 5, 6, 8, 9 with median 6, so the first quartile is 6. The upper five are 11, 12, 14, 15, 20 with median 14. The interquartile range is $14 - 6 = 8$.

questions.stem: In a data set, the largest value is made much larger and stays above the third quartile. Which summary does NOT change?
choices: The range
The interquartile range
The mean
The standard deviation
questions.answer: The interquartile range
questions.solution: The interquartile range depends only on the first and third quartiles, which do not move. The range, the mean and the standard deviation all use the largest value, so they increase.

solve.answer: The interquartile range
solve.work: Q1 and Q3 do not depend on how large the maximum is (it stays above Q3); mean, SD, range all change.

questions.stem: Five values are 1, 1, 3, 5 and 5. Treat them as a sample and find the sample standard deviation: divide the sum of the squared deviations from the mean by $n - 1$, then take the square root. What is the standard deviation?
questions.solution: The mean is 3. The deviations are $-2, -2, 0, 2, 2$, with squares 4, 4, 0, 4, 4, which add to 16. Divide by $5 - 1 = 4$ to get 4, and the square root is 2.

solve.work: Mean 3; squared deviations 4,4,0,4,4 = 16; 16/4 = 4; sqrt 4 = 2.

questions.stem: A sample has 9 values. The squared deviations from the mean add up to 72. What is the sample standard deviation, which uses $n - 1$?
questions.solution: Divide by $n - 1 = 8$: $\frac{72}{8} = 9$. The standard deviation is the square root of 9, which is 3.

questions.stem: Which of these CANNOT be the standard deviation of a data set?
questions.solution: A standard deviation is a square root of an average of squares, so it is never negative. It can be 0 if all values are equal, and it can be any non-negative number.

solve.work: SD is a square root, never negative: -3.

questions.stem: On a test the mean is 100 and the standard deviation is 15. A student scored 85. What is the student's z-score?
questions.solution: $z = \frac{85 - 100}{15} = -1$. The score is 1 standard deviation below the mean.

questions.stem: Which value is more unusual for its distribution: a value with a z-score of 2.5, or one with a z-score of $-1.8$?
choices: The z-score of $-1.8$, because negative values are always unusual
They are equally unusual, because one is positive and the other is negative
The z-score of $-1.8$, because its distance from 0 is the larger one
The z-score of 2.5, because it is farther from the mean
questions.answer: The z-score of 2.5, because it is farther from the mean
questions.solution: How unusual a value is depends on the distance of its z-score from 0. Since $2.5 > 1.8$, the z-score of 2.5 is farther from the mean.

solve.answer: The z-score of 2.5, because it is farther from the mean
solve.work: |2.5| > |-1.8|, so 2.5 is farther from the mean.

questions.stem: Ben's score is at the 35th percentile in a group of 60 students. About how many students scored at or below Ben's score?
questions.solution: At the 35th percentile, 35% of the group scored at or below: $0.35 \times 60 = 21$ students.

questions.stem: A test score of 72 is at the 50th percentile. Which statement must be true?
choices: About half of the students scored at or below 72
About half of the students scored exactly 72
The mean score on the test is 72
The student answered half of the questions correctly
questions.answer: About half of the students scored at or below 72
questions.solution: The 50th percentile means about 50% of the group is at or below that score. It does not say how many scored exactly 72, what the mean is, or what fraction of the questions was right.

solve.answer: About half of the students scored at or below 72
solve.work: 50th percentile: about half at or below 72.

questions.stem: Eight scores in order are 60, 64, 66, 70, 80, 84, 86 and 90. Find the quartiles as the medians of the lower four values and the upper four values. A value is a low outlier if it is below Q1 - 1.5 x IQR. What is this lower cutoff?
questions.solution: The lower four are 60, 64, 66, 70, so $Q_1 = \frac{64+66}{2} = 65$. The upper four are 80, 84, 86, 90, so $Q_3 = \frac{84+86}{2} = 85$. The IQR is 20, and $65 - 1.5 \times 20 = 35$.

questions.stem: While studying a data set, a student finds an outlier. What should she do first?
choices: Remove it at once, because every outlier is a mistake in the data
Find out why it differs, and remove it only if it is an error
Keep it and ignore it, because one value cannot matter at all
Replace it with the mean of all of the other values
questions.answer: Find out why it differs, and remove it only if it is an error
questions.solution: An outlier may be a data-entry error or a real, important value. It should be investigated and removed only with a good reason, not simply because it is extreme.

solve.answer: Find out why it differs, and remove it only if it is an error
solve.work: Investigate first; remove only if an error.

questions.stem: A very large outlier is added to a data set that is roughly symmetric. Which result is most likely?
choices: The median rises sharply, but the mean barely moves at all
The mean and the median both stay exactly the same as before
The mean and standard deviation rise sharply, but the median barely moves
The standard deviation decreases, because there are now more values
questions.answer: The mean and standard deviation rise sharply, but the median barely moves
questions.solution: The mean and the standard deviation use every value, so a very large one pulls them up. The median depends on the middle of the ordered data and moves very little.

solve.answer: The mean and standard deviation rise sharply, but the median barely moves
solve.work: Mean and SD are sensitive to an outlier; median is resistant.

questions.stem: A shoe store wants to decide which shoe size to stock the most of. Which measure of center is most useful?
choices: The mean, the average of all the sizes
The median, the middle of all the sizes
The range, the spread of all the sizes
The mode, the size that is most common
questions.answer: The mode, the size that is most common
questions.solution: The store needs the size that is bought most often, which is the mode. A mean size such as 8.3 may not even be a real shoe size.

solve.answer: The mode, the size that is most common
solve.work: Most common size: mode.

questions.stem: Class A scored with a first quartile of 60, a median of 70 and a third quartile of 80. Class B scored with a first quartile of 55, a median of 70 and a third quartile of 90. Which statement is supported?
choices: The medians are equal, but Class B is more spread out in the middle
Class B has a higher median than Class A does
Class A is more spread out in its middle half than Class B
Class A has a larger range than Class B
questions.answer: The medians are equal, but Class B is more spread out in the middle
questions.solution: The medians are both 70. The interquartile range is 20 for Class A and 35 for Class B, so Class B is more spread out in its middle half. The ranges cannot be compared from these numbers.

solve.answer: The medians are equal, but Class B is more spread out in the middle
solve.work: Medians both 70; IQR A = 20, B = 35.

questions.stem: Delivery company A has a median delivery time of 20 minutes with an interquartile range of 4 minutes. Company B has a median of 24 minutes with an interquartile range of 4 minutes. Which statement is supported?
choices: Company B is typically faster, and the two are about equally consistent
Company A is typically faster, and the two are about equally consistent
Company A is typically faster, and Company A is less consistent
Company B is typically faster, and Company B is more consistent
questions.answer: Company A is typically faster, and the two are about equally consistent
questions.solution: A lower median time is a faster typical delivery, so Company A is faster. The equal interquartile ranges show equal spread, so the two are about equally consistent.

solve.answer: Company A is typically faster, and the two are about equally consistent
solve.work: A median 20 < 24 (faster); equal IQRs (equally consistent).

questions.stem: In a distribution that is skewed to the right, how do the mean and the median compare?
choices: The mean is less than the median
The mean is equal to the median
The mean is greater than the median
The mean cannot be compared with the median
questions.answer: The mean is greater than the median
questions.solution: The long tail of larger values pulls the mean upward more than the median, so in a right-skewed distribution the mean is greater than the median.

solve.answer: The mean is greater than the median
solve.work: Right skew pulls the mean above the median.

questions.stem: Test scores have a mean of 60 and a standard deviation of 8. Every score is multiplied by 1.5. What is the new standard deviation?
questions.solution: Multiplying every value by 1.5 multiplies the standard deviation by 1.5 as well: $8 \times 1.5 = 12$.

solve.work: SD scales by 1.5: 8 x 1.5 = 12.

questions.stem: The scores on an exam have a first quartile of 42 and a third quartile of 58, so the interquartile range is 16. Which is the best interpretation of the 16?
choices: All of the scores are within 16 points of each other
16% of the students scored between 42 and 58
The highest score is 16 points above the lowest score
The middle half of the scores spans 16 points
questions.answer: The middle half of the scores spans 16 points
questions.solution: The interquartile range is the width of the interval holding the middle 50% of the data. Here that interval, from 42 to 58, is 16 points wide.

solve.answer: The middle half of the scores spans 16 points
solve.work: IQR is the width of the middle half.

questions.stem: Among girls her age, Maria's height has a z-score of 2.1. Which is the best interpretation?
choices: Her height is 2.1 standard deviations above the mean
Her height is 2.1 centimeters above the mean height
She is taller than only 2.1% of the girls her age
Her height is 2.1 times the mean height of girls her age
questions.answer: Her height is 2.1 standard deviations above the mean
questions.solution: A z-score counts standard deviations from the mean. A z-score of 2.1 means her height is 2.1 standard deviations above the mean.

solve.answer: Her height is 2.1 standard deviations above the mean
solve.work: z = 2.1: 2.1 SDs above the mean.

questions.stem: Eight deliveries took 4, 6, 7, 9, 10, 12, 13 and 40 minutes. Find the quartiles as the medians of the lower four values and the upper four values. A value is a high outlier if it is above Q3 + 1.5 x IQR. What is this cutoff?
questions.solution: The lower four values 4, 6, 7, 9 give Q1 = (6 + 7) / 2 = 6.5. The upper four values 10, 12, 13, 40 give Q3 = (12 + 13) / 2 = 12.5. IQR = 12.5 - 6.5 = 6. The cutoff is 12.5 + 1.5 x 6 = 21.5, so the 40-minute delivery is an outlier.

questions.stem: Temperatures in a city, measured in degrees Celsius, have a mean of 20 and a standard deviation of 5. Each temperature is converted to Fahrenheit using F = 1.8C + 32. What is the standard deviation of the temperatures in degrees Fahrenheit?
questions.solution: Adding 32 shifts every value but does not change the spread. Multiplying by 1.8 stretches the spread by 1.8, so the standard deviation is 1.8 x 5 = 9.

solve.work: Adding 32 does not change spread; multiplying by 1.8 multiplies SD by 1.8. 1.8 x 5 = 9.

questions.stem: On an exam with a mean of 540, a score of 590 has a z-score of 1.25. What is the standard deviation of the exam scores?
questions.solution: The score is 590 - 540 = 50 points above the mean, and that is 1.25 standard deviations. One standard deviation is 50 / 1.25 = 40.

questions.stem: One class of 20 students has a mean quiz score of 70. Another class of 30 students has a mean score of 80 on the same quiz. What is the mean score of all 50 students?
questions.solution: The first class has a total of 20 x 70 = 1,400 points and the second 30 x 80 = 2,400 points. Together that is 3,800 points for 50 students: 3,800 / 50 = 76. (It is not 75, because the larger class counts more.)

questions.stem: Four quiz scores are 72, 85, 90 and 77. What score on the fifth quiz would give a mean of exactly 82 over all five quizzes?
questions.solution: A mean of 82 over five quizzes needs a total of 5 x 82 = 410. The first four total 72 + 85 + 90 + 77 = 324. The fifth score must be 410 - 324 = 86.

questions.stem: Maya scored 78 on a test with a mean of 70 and a standard deviation of 4. Leo scored 84 on a different test with a mean of 74 and a standard deviation of 10. Who did better compared with the other students who took the same test?
choices: Leo, because his score of 84 is higher than Maya's score of 78
Maya, because her z-score of 2 is higher than Leo's z-score of 1
Leo, because he is 10 points above his mean and Maya is 8 above hers
They did equally well, because each scored above the mean of their test
questions.answer: Maya, because her z-score of 2 is higher than Leo's z-score of 1
questions.solution: Compare z-scores. Maya: (78 - 70) / 4 = 2. Leo: (84 - 74) / 10 = 1. Maya is 2 standard deviations above her mean and Leo only 1, so Maya did better relative to her test.

solve.answer: Maya, because her z-score of 2 is higher than Leo's z-score of 1
solve.work: Maya z = (78-70)/4 = 2. Leo z = (84-74)/10 = 1. Maya is further above her mean relative to spread.

questions.stem: Data set A has a mean of 50 and a median of 50. Data set B has a mean of 62 and a median of 49. Which statement about their shapes is best supported?
choices: A is roughly symmetric, and B is skewed to the left
A is skewed to the right, and B is roughly symmetric
A and B are both roughly symmetric
A is roughly symmetric, and B is skewed to the right
questions.answer: A is roughly symmetric, and B is skewed to the right
questions.solution: When the mean and median are equal the distribution is roughly symmetric. When the mean is well above the median, a long tail of large values pulls the mean up, which is a skew to the right.

solve.answer: A is roughly symmetric, and B is skewed to the right
solve.work: A: mean = median, consistent with roughly symmetric. B: mean 62 well above median 49, pulled up by high values: skewed right.

questions.stem: All four data sets below have a mean of 6. Without calculating, which one has the largest standard deviation?
choices: Data set A: 4, 5, 6, 7, 8
Data set C: 6, 6, 6, 6, 6
Data set D: 5, 5, 6, 7, 7
Data set B: 2, 3, 6, 9, 10
questions.answer: Data set B: 2, 3, 6, 9, 10
questions.solution: The standard deviation grows as the values lie farther from the mean. Set B has values 4 away from the mean of 6, while the other sets have values within 2 of the mean (sum of squared deviations: B 50, A 10, D 4, C 0).

solve.answer: Data set B: 2, 3, 6, 9, 10
solve.work: Distances from 6: B 4,3,0,3,4; A 2,1,0,1,2; D 1,1,0,1,1; C all 0. B is most spread out, so largest SD.

questions.stem: Every value in a data set is increased by 10. Which statement about the mean and the standard deviation is correct?
choices: The mean and the standard deviation both increase by 10
The mean increases by 10, and the standard deviation stays the same
The mean stays the same, and the standard deviation increases by 10
The mean and the standard deviation both stay the same
questions.answer: The mean increases by 10, and the standard deviation stays the same
questions.solution: Adding 10 to every value shifts the whole distribution up by 10, so the mean goes up by 10. The distances between values do not change, so the spread, and the standard deviation, stay the same.

solve.answer: The mean increases by 10, and the standard deviation stays the same
solve.work: Adding a constant shifts the centre by 10 but leaves distances from the mean unchanged, so SD stays the same.

questions.stem: Two data sets have the same range. Set A has an interquartile range of 5 and Set B has an interquartile range of 20. Which statement is best supported?
choices: The middle half of Set B is packed more tightly than the middle half of Set A
Set A must have the larger standard deviation
The middle half of Set A is packed more tightly than the middle half of Set B
Set A and Set B have the same spread, because their ranges are equal
questions.answer: The middle half of Set A is packed more tightly than the middle half of Set B
questions.solution: The interquartile range measures the spread of the middle half of the data. A smaller interquartile range means the middle half of Set A is closer together. Equal ranges do not mean equal spread elsewhere.

solve.answer: The middle half of Set A is packed more tightly than the middle half of Set B
solve.work: IQR is the spread of the middle half: A's IQR 5 < B's 20, so A's middle half is packed more tightly. Same range does not mean same spread; SD cannot be deduced.

questions.stem: The mean of 5 values is 14. A sixth value is added, and the mean of all 6 values is 16. What is the sixth value?
questions.solution: The first 5 values add to $5 \times 14 = 70$. All 6 add to $6 \times 16 = 96$. The sixth value is $96 - 70 = 26$.

questions.stem: A group of 12 students has a mean score of 50. A second group has 8 students. The mean score of all 20 students together is 53. What is the mean score of the second group?
questions.solution: All 20 students total $20 \times 53 = 1060$. The first group totals $12 \times 50 = 600$, so the second totals 460. Its mean is $\frac{460}{8} = 57.5$.

questions.stem: Six values in order are 3, 5, 8, b, 14 and 20, and their median is 9.5. What is b?
questions.solution: With six values the median is the mean of the third and fourth: $\frac{8 + b}{2} = 9.5$. So $8 + b = 19$ and $b = 11$.

solve.work: Median = (8+b)/2 = 9.5 -> b = 11 (between 8 and 14, consistent with order).

questions.stem: In a survey of 20 students, 4 have 0 siblings, 9 have 1 sibling, 5 have 2 siblings and 2 have 3 siblings. What is the median number of siblings?
questions.solution: With 20 values the median is the mean of the 10th and 11th values in order. The first 4 values are 0 and the next 9 are 1, so the 5th through 13th values are 1. Both middle values are 1, so the median is 1.

solve.work: 20 values: 10th and 11th. Positions 1-4 are 0, 5-13 are 1; median 1.

questions.stem: Twelve values in order are 1, 3, 4, 6, 7, 9, 10, 12, 13, 15, 18 and 22. Find the quartiles as the medians of the lower six values and the upper six values. What is the interquartile range?
questions.solution: The lower six are 1, 3, 4, 6, 7, 9, with median $\frac{4+6}{2} = 5$. The upper six are 10, 12, 13, 15, 18, 22, with median $\frac{13+15}{2} = 14$. The interquartile range is $14 - 5 = 9$.

questions.stem: A data set has a minimum of 12, a first quartile of 30, a median of 38, a third quartile of 52 and a maximum of 95. How much larger is its range than its interquartile range?
questions.solution: The range is $95 - 12 = 83$ and the interquartile range is $52 - 30 = 22$. The difference is $83 - 22 = 61$.

questions.stem: Which description of a data set is impossible?
choices: An interquartile range of 25 with a range of 30
An interquartile range of 30 with a range of 25
An interquartile range of 0 with a range of 10
An interquartile range of 10 with a range of 10
questions.answer: An interquartile range of 30 with a range of 25
questions.solution: The quartiles lie between the minimum and the maximum, so the interquartile range can never exceed the range. It can equal the range, or be 0 when the middle half of the data are all equal.

solve.answer: An interquartile range of 30 with a range of 25
solve.work: IQR lies within the range, so IQR cannot exceed range: IQR 30 with range 25 is impossible. IQR 10 = range 10 is possible (e.g. 0,0,10,10).

questions.stem: A whole population has the 8 values 2, 4, 4, 4, 5, 5, 7 and 9, with a mean of 5. For a whole population, divide the sum of the squared deviations by $n$ (not $n - 1$) and take the square root. What is the population standard deviation?
questions.solution: The deviations are $-3, -1, -1, -1, 0, 0, 2, 4$, with squares 9, 1, 1, 1, 0, 0, 4, 16, which add to 32. Divide by 8 to get 4, and the square root is 2.

solve.work: Squared deviations 9,1,1,1,0,0,4,16 = 32; 32/8 = 4; sqrt = 2.

questions.stem: A new value equal to the mean is added to a data set. What happens to the mean and the standard deviation?
choices: The mean stays the same and the standard deviation stays the same
The mean gets smaller and the standard deviation gets smaller
The mean stays the same and the standard deviation gets smaller
The mean stays the same and the standard deviation gets larger
questions.answer: The mean stays the same and the standard deviation gets smaller
questions.solution: A value equal to the mean adds nothing to the sum of squared deviations but increases the number of values. The mean is unchanged and the standard deviation shrinks slightly.

solve.answer: The mean stays the same and the standard deviation gets smaller
solve.work: Mean unchanged; sum of squared deviations unchanged while n grows, so SD shrinks (edge case: if SD was already 0 it stays 0).

questions.stem: On one test, a score of 83 has a z-score of 0.5 and a score of 95 has a z-score of 2. What is the mean score on the test?
questions.solution: The two scores differ by $95 - 83 = 12$ points, which is $2 - 0.5 = 1.5$ standard deviations, so one standard deviation is 8 points. The score 83 is 0.5 standard deviations (4 points) above the mean, so the mean is $83 - 4 = 79$.

questions.stem: A 7-year-old boy is 135 centimeters tall, and boys his age have a mean height of 120 and a standard deviation of 6. A 40-year-old man is 195 centimeters tall, and men his age have a mean height of 178 and a standard deviation of 8. Whose height is more unusual for his group?
choices: The man, because he is 17 centimeters above his mean and the boy only 15
The man, because 195 is greater than 135
They are equally unusual, because both are taller than average
The boy, with a z-score of 2.5 against 2.125 for the man
questions.answer: The boy, with a z-score of 2.5 against 2.125 for the man
questions.solution: Compare z-scores. For the boy $z = \frac{135 - 120}{6} = 2.5$. For the man $z = \frac{195 - 178}{8} = 2.125$. The boy's score is farther from his group's mean.

solve.answer: The boy, with a z-score of 2.5 against 2.125 for the man

questions.stem: A score of 640 is at the 85th percentile among 300 students. About how many of the students scored above 640?
questions.solution: About 85% scored at or below 640, so about 15% scored above: $0.15 \times 300 = 45$ students.

solve.work: 15% of 300 = 45 above.

questions.stem: Kira's score is at the 30th percentile of a test, and her friend's score is at the 60th percentile of the same test. Which statement is correct?
choices: Her friend scored higher than Kira, but not necessarily twice as high
Her friend's score is exactly twice as high as Kira's
Her friend answered exactly 60% of the questions correctly
Kira's score is higher than her friend's, because 30 is less than 60
questions.answer: Her friend scored higher than Kira, but not necessarily twice as high
questions.solution: A higher percentile means a higher score relative to the group. Percentiles are positions, not points, so one cannot say the score is twice as high or what fraction of the questions was correct.

solve.answer: Her friend scored higher than Kira, but not necessarily twice as high
solve.work: Percentile is rank, not proportional to score; friend higher, not necessarily double.

questions.stem: Eight values in order are 3, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10 and 30. Find the quartiles as the medians of the lower four values and the upper four values. How many of the values are outliers by the rule that a value is an outlier if it is more than 1.5 x IQR below Q1 or above Q3?
questions.solution: $Q_1 = \frac{5+6}{2} = 5.5$ and $Q_3 = \frac{9+10}{2} = 9.5$, so the IQR is 4 and $1.5 \times 4 = 6$. The cutoffs are $5.5 - 6 = -0.5$ and $9.5 + 6 = 15.5$. Only 30 is outside them, so there is 1 outlier.

solve.work: Q1 = (5+6)/2 = 5.5, Q3 = (9+10)/2 = 9.5, IQR 4; fences -0.5 and 15.5; only 30 is an outlier.

questions.stem: The largest value in a data set, which is far above all the others, is removed. What is the most likely effect?
choices: The median decreases a lot, and the mean and standard deviation change little
The mean and standard deviation drop a lot, and the median changes little
The mean decreases, and the standard deviation increases because of the smaller count
None of the three summaries changes at all, because only one value was removed
questions.answer: The mean and standard deviation drop a lot, and the median changes little
questions.solution: The extreme value affected the mean and standard deviation strongly, so removing it lowers both. The median depends on the middle of the ordered data and changes little.

solve.answer: The mean and standard deviation drop a lot, and the median changes little
solve.work: Removing a far outlier drops mean and SD a lot; median shifts little.

questions.stem: A company reports that its mean salary is 90,000 dollars, while its median salary is 55,000 dollars, because a few executives are paid very high salaries. Which value better describes a typical employee's salary, and why?
choices: The mean, because it uses every salary in the company
The mean, because it is larger than the median is
The median, because a few high salaries pull the mean up
The median, because it is smaller than the mean is
questions.answer: The median, because a few high salaries pull the mean up
questions.solution: A few very high salaries inflate the mean, but the median is resistant to them, so it describes the middle employee better.

solve.answer: The median, because a few high salaries pull the mean up
solve.work: Median resists the few large salaries that pull the mean up.

questions.stem: The ages of the visitors to a park form two separate peaks, one of children and one of older adults. A report gives only the mean and the standard deviation. Why could this mislead?
choices: The mean and standard deviation cannot be calculated for ages of people
The mean is always larger than the median for any ages
The standard deviation is always 0 when there are two groups
One center and one spread hide two separate groups of visitors
questions.answer: One center and one spread hide two separate groups of visitors
questions.solution: A single center and spread suggest one group clustered around the mean, which here may fall where few visitors actually are. A histogram would show the two peaks.

solve.answer: One center and one spread hide two separate groups of visitors
solve.work: A bimodal distribution is badly described by one centre and spread.

questions.stem: Data set X and data set Y both have a mean of 50 and a standard deviation of 10. X is roughly symmetric, and Y is strongly skewed to the right. Which statement is correct?
choices: The same mean and spread do not give the same shape
The two data sets must also have exactly the same median
The two data sets must also have exactly the same shape
Y must also have a smaller range than X does
questions.answer: The same mean and spread do not give the same shape
questions.solution: The mean and standard deviation do not describe shape. Data sets with the same two values can look very different, and the skewed one will usually have a median below its mean.

solve.answer: The same mean and spread do not give the same shape
solve.work: Same mean and SD can have different shapes.

questions.stem: Class P has a minimum of 40, Q1 of 60, median of 70, Q3 of 80 and maximum of 100. Class Q has a minimum of 55, Q1 of 65, median of 72, Q3 of 78 and maximum of 90. Which statement is supported?
choices: Class P has a narrower middle half, and Q has a wider range
Class Q has a narrower middle half, and P has a wider range
Class P has the higher median and the narrower range
The two classes have the same spread, since both medians are near 70
questions.answer: Class Q has a narrower middle half, and P has a wider range
questions.solution: The IQR is 20 for P and 13 for Q, so Q's middle half is narrower. The range is 60 for P and 35 for Q, so P's overall range is wider. Q's median, 72, is also slightly higher.

solve.answer: Class Q has a narrower middle half, and P has a wider range
solve.work: P: IQR 20, range 60; Q: IQR 13, range 35. Q narrower middle half; P wider range.

questions.stem: A data set has a mean of 38 and a median of 45. Which statement about its shape is best supported?
choices: It is probably skewed to the right
It is exactly symmetric
It is probably skewed to the left
It must have no outliers
questions.answer: It is probably skewed to the left
questions.solution: The mean is pulled toward a long tail. A mean below the median suggests a tail toward the smaller values, which is a skew to the left.

solve.answer: It is probably skewed to the left
solve.work: Mean below median suggests a left tail.

questions.stem: Scores out of 50 have a mean of 30 and a standard deviation of 6. Mia scored 39. All scores are doubled so that they are out of 100. What is Mia's z-score on the doubled scores?
questions.solution: Doubling changes the mean to 60, the standard deviation to 12 and Mia's score to 78. Her z-score is $\frac{78 - 60}{12} = 1.5$, which is the same as before: $\frac{39 - 30}{6} = 1.5$. A z-score does not change under a change of units.

solve.work: z = (39-30)/6 = 1.5; doubling all scores doubles mean and SD, z unchanged: 1.5.

questions.stem: Temperatures in degrees Fahrenheit have a standard deviation of 9. They were converted from degrees Celsius with F = 1.8C + 32. What was the standard deviation in degrees Celsius?
questions.solution: Adding 32 does not change the spread, and multiplying by 1.8 multiplies the standard deviation by 1.8. So the Celsius standard deviation is $9 \div 1.8 = 5$.

solve.work: SD_F = 1.8 SD_C (shift does not matter): 9/1.8 = 5.

questions.stem: Lena says, "My score has a z-score of $-0.4$, so I did badly." Which is the best response?
choices: She is right, because any negative z-score means a poor score
Her score is 0.4 points below the mean score on the test
She scored lower than 40% of the students who took it
Her score is 0.4 standard deviations below the mean, near average
questions.answer: Her score is 0.4 standard deviations below the mean, near average
questions.solution: A z-score of $-0.4$ is less than half a standard deviation below the mean, which is close to the middle of the group, not a bad result.

solve.answer: Her score is 0.4 standard deviations below the mean, near average
solve.work: z = -0.4: 0.4 SD below the mean, close to average.

questions.skill: Interpret and use a linear model
questions.stem: A model predicts a student's test score from the hours studied: $S = 52 + 6h$, where $S$ is the predicted score and $h$ is the number of hours studied. What does the 6 mean?
choices: Each extra hour of study adds 6 points to the predicted score
A student who studies 0 hours is predicted to score 6 points
A student who studies 6 hours is predicted to score 52 points
The predicted score goes up by 6 percent for each hour studied
questions.answer: Each extra hour of study adds 6 points to the predicted score
questions.solution: In $S = 52 + 6h$ the number multiplying $h$ is the slope. It is the change in the predicted score for each extra hour. So each extra hour adds 6 points. The 52 is the predicted score for 0 hours.

solve.answer: Each extra hour of study adds 6 points to the predicted score
solve.work: In S = 52 + 6h the coefficient 6 is the slope: each additional hour of study raises the predicted score by 6 points. 52 is the intercept.

questions.stem: A model for the number of tiles in the $n$th pattern of a tile design is $T = n^2 + 3n$. How many tiles does the model give for pattern 5?
questions.solution: Put $n = 5$ into the model: $T = 5^2 + 3 \times 5 = 25 + 15 = 40$ tiles.

questions.stem: The population of a town is modeled by $P = 200 \cdot 1.05^t$, where $t$ is the number of years from now. By what percent does the population grow each year?
choices: 105 percent
5 percent
1.05 percent
0.05 percent
questions.answer: 5 percent
questions.solution: In $P = a \cdot b^t$ the growth factor is $b = 1.05$. Each year the population is multiplied by 1.05, which is the old amount plus 0.05 of it. So it grows by 5 percent each year.

solve.answer: 5 percent
solve.work: Growth factor 1.05 = 1 + 0.05, so growth rate is 5% per year.

questions.stem: A bacteria culture is modeled by $N = 500 \cdot 2^t$, where $t$ is the number of hours. How many bacteria does the model give after 3 hours?
questions.solution: Put $t = 3$ into the model: $N = 500 \cdot 2^3 = 500 \times 8 = 4000$ bacteria.

questions.stem: A line predicts that a plant will be 24 centimeters tall after 6 weeks. The plant actually measures 27 centimeters. What is the residual, found as actual minus predicted, in centimeters?
questions.solution: A residual is the actual value minus the predicted value: $27 - 24 = 3$ centimeters. It is positive because the plant is taller than the line predicted.

solve.work: Residual = actual - predicted = 27 - 24 = 3.

questions.stem: On a test, the mean score is 70 and the standard deviation is 5. Maya scored 80. What is her z-score?
questions.solution: A z-score is $\frac{\text{score} - \text{mean}}{\text{standard deviation}}$. Here $z = \frac{80 - 70}{5} = \frac{10}{5} = 2$. Maya's score is 2 standard deviations above the mean.

questions.stem: The number of students who have heard a rumor in a school of 500 students is modeled by a logistic function. What happens to this number as time goes on?
choices: It keeps growing faster and faster with no upper limit
It falls steadily until no one has heard the rumor
It grows quickly at first, then levels off near 500
It grows by exactly the same amount every day forever
questions.answer: It grows quickly at first, then levels off near 500
questions.solution: A logistic curve is S-shaped. It starts slowly, speeds up, and then levels off at a maximum, here the 500 students in the school. Nobody can hear the rumor twice, so the number cannot grow without limit.

solve.answer: It grows quickly at first, then levels off near 500
solve.issues: Minor: a rumor's logistic curve usually starts slowly, speeds up, then levels off (S-shape); "grows quickly at first" is a simplification, though it is still the only defensible option.
solve.work: Logistic growth rises toward a carrying capacity, here the 500 students, and levels off near it. Other options describe linear, exponential or decay.

questions.stem: A fair coin is flipped 3 times. What is the probability of getting exactly 2 heads?
questions.solution: There are 3 ways to get exactly 2 heads in 3 flips: HHT, HTH and THH. Each way has probability $\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^3 = \frac{1}{8}$. So the probability is $3 \times \frac{1}{8} = \frac{3}{8}$.

questions.stem: The heights of adult women are approximately normal with a mean of 64 inches and a standard deviation of 3 inches. About what percent of these women are between 61 and 67 inches tall?
choices: 34 percent
95 percent
99.7 percent
68 percent
questions.answer: 68 percent
